terra.problem: Referring to the last few passages assumes the baker knows earlier lessons. Each lesson stands on its own.
The text says evening, not that Aaron starts precisely when the sun goes down.
The text does not say that starting at midnight would leave the lamps in darkness for a long gap.
The passage does not say nobody needs help seeing at noon or give darkness as the reason for the stated hours.
Papa's backstory describes his own edges wearing down over years, not several of his stamps wearing out in a few years.

The claim about the bronze altar is outside this passage and needs its own reference. The joke about keeping loaves away from anything that burns also uses bread as a joke rather than as a Bible fact.
The passage says the loaves are on the table, but does not say they are in plain view or contrast their placement with hiding them.
Calling the Sabbath a day of rest brings in a fact from outside this passage without a reference.
The passage says the bread is set out every Sabbath; it does not specify fifty-some batches or say the ovens never get cold.
The claim that the new moon is a marker of time in the Bible is outside this passage and needs a reference.
The explanation is generic, and its closing line about not adding to the text has little of Papa's voice.
The explanation is generic, and its closing line about sticking with the text has little of Papa's voice.
The text requires a holy place, but does not say whether a tent could be one.
The closing joke calls the bread a snack. Scripture's food exception permits mentioning bread as a Bible fact, not using it as food in a joke.
The text requires a holy place, but does not say that the tents are excluded. It also does not say Aaron and his sons were tempted to take the bread elsewhere.
